jalaur-dam-tumandok-killings.conditions_add: The borrower's own project site says Korea Eximbank's concurrence to the Stage II construction contract was given on 19 November 2019, quoting KEXIM's letter: "We kindly notify you that the subject contract has been approved by us in accordance with Section 6.03 of the General Terms and Conditions Applicable to EDCF Loan Agreement" (National Irrigation Administration, JRMP II). The same page says that in securing that concurrence "Certain environmental and social requirements have to be complied by the project proponent", that stakeholder involvement and the safety of people with affected properties "are the main concerns of the funding institution", and that the project's "Fund for the project is from a tied-loan with the Government of South Korea through its EDCF". A Minutes of Discussion signed with EDCF-KEXIM on 4 September 2015 covers "compliance of NIA on Environmental and Social (E&S) measures prior to the commencement of construction of the project" (NIA). The loan was approved on 9 August 2012 and took effect on 28 November 2012.

why.admin: the subject contract has been approved by us in accordance with Section 6.03 of the General Terms and Conditions Applicable to EDCF Loan Agreement
why.safeguard: "Certain environmental and social requirements have to be complied by the project proponent"
why.tied: "Fund for the project is from a tied-loan with the Government of South Korea through its EDCF"

sources_add.publisher: National Irrigation Administration, Jalaur River Multipurpose Project

sources_add.title: NIA Signs Minutes of Discussion with EDCF-KEXIM

jalaur-dam-tumandok-killings.searched: Checked against the borrower's own loan-administration pages, opened in full: the JRMP II page carries KEXIM's letter citing Section 6.03 of the General Terms and Conditions of the EDCF Loan Agreement as the basis for approving the construction contract, the environmental and social requirements that had to be complied with to get that concurrence, and the description of the money as a tied loan; the NIA page on the 2015 Minutes of Discussion gives the E&S measures 'prior to the commencement of construction' and the loan's approval and effective dates. The loan agreement text itself is not published.

bataan-nuclear-plant-debt.conditions_add: The President of the US Export-Import Bank, John L. Moore Jr., told a Senate Finance subcommittee on 23 January 1978 that the Philippine nuclear plant credit was a loan where money was raised "by Eximbank extending its guarantees to bonds of the Philippine Government to raise money to pay for the nuclear plant", and that "the total amount of loans and guarantees was in the range of $600 million to $700 million". Asked about commission payments on the contract, he said: "Under our procedures, disbursements of the loan would not go to the Philippines, but only to the exporters in the United States against proof of export of the particular items." He also said each loan is analysed for the appropriateness of the figures and that "affidavits are taken from the borrower and the exporter stating what payments are being made in connection with the transaction", and that "Both procedures were followed in the case of the Philippines". This is the Bank president's account of the Bank's own procedures as applied to this credit; no clause of the credit or guarantee agreement is published.

why.tied: "Under our procedures, disbursements of the loan would not go to the Philippines, but only to the exporters in the United States against proof of export of the particular items."

sources_add.title: Foreign Indebtedness to the United States: hearing before the Subcommittee on Taxation and Debt Management Generally, Committee on Finance, United States Senate, 23 January 1978

bataan-nuclear-plant-debt.searched: The whole 1978 Senate Finance hearing 'Foreign Indebtedness to the United States' was read, not just its opening: the PDF was converted to text (432,000 characters) and every mention of 'Philippines' and 'nuclear' checked. The Eximbank president's exchange with Senator Byrd at pages 18-22 is the only passage on this credit; it gives the structure, the size and the disbursement rule, and nothing further on terms appears anywhere else in the transcript. The quotations here are from clean passages; parts of the OCR elsewhere are garbled. No credit agreement, guarantee agreement or Eximbank authorisation document for the Philippine transaction is published.

salonga-wwf-ecoguards-usaid-kfw.searched: The KfW La Salonga paper was opened in full on entwicklungsbank.kfw.de and carries no term of the Salonga agreements. Its sentence "German development cooperation emphasises that it does not finance the provision of arms for ecoguards" sits in the Background section as a general position of German development cooperation, not as a clause of this financing; the environmental and social due diligence assessment, the grievance mechanism (4.9.2) and the executing agency's reporting duties are set out in the paper's section 7 as provisions of KfW's general Sustainability Guideline, and the human rights impact assessment is discretionary ("may require"). The paper records only that "KfW signed a consultancy agreement with WWF on behalf of the Congolese partner authority ICCN" and says nothing about that agreement's terms. No USAID award document or cooperative agreement for Salonga was found.

path-hpv-khammam-vadodara.searched: Opened the 72nd Report of the Indian Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health (2013) in full. It records only that the projects were "reportedly funded by Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation" (paras 1.1 and 6.27), that "no information had been provided to Indian authorities about funding of the project" (para 6.27) and that no figure for the total outlay is available (para 6.28). The only agreement it sets out is the PATH-ICMR memorandum of understanding of 20 February 2007, which lists project purposes and does not mention the foundation. No grant agreement or funder term exists in the record.

sources_add.title: 72nd Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare on alleged irregularities in the conduct of studies using HPV vaccine by PATH in India

theun-hinboun-expansion.searched: Went to the development financiers' own disclosure instead of BankTrack: FMO's only published Theun-Hinboun record (project 55227, and its ewsdata.rightsindevelopment.org mirror) is a EUR 0.10 million facility approved 4 December 2018 to train resettled farmers in crop rotation, not the 2009 US$112.5 million loan; it gives an E&S category A and no action plan, covenant or condition. No DEG or Proparco disclosure for the 2008-09 syndicated loan was found.

xe-pian-xe-namnoy-collapse.searched: Searched in Korean for the EDCF loan contract and the reported US$4.8 million early-filling bonus through Korean trade and news hosts; no Korea Eximbank EDCF loan document, National Assembly audit paper or Lao ratification text for the October 2015 US$80.8 million loan was found, and nothing on the Thai banks' March 2014 US$700 million facility to Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy Power Company. Correction to the earlier note: peoplepower21.org is not a refusing host - its homepage serves in full - the failure was that the particular PSPD article pages returned a redirect script instead of their text.

xayaburi-dam-thai-banks.searched: The TRIS Rating report was opened and does say "The project loans incorporate a cash waterfall mechanism to reserve cash for planned maintenance expenses and debt repayment" and that "The conditions of project loans ensures that XPCL will have sufficient liquidity" "to meet principal repayment and interest expenses for the next six months". It cannot be used here: the report is dated 27 December 2024 and describes THB61.7 billion of loans outstanding in September 2024, names no lender and gives no signing date, so nothing ties the mechanism to the 2010-2012 Thai syndicate whose money built the dam and paid for the resettlement; and a cash waterfall with a six-month debt service reserve is an ordinary project-finance mechanic rather than a requirement on how the money was used. The syndicated loan agreement itself is still unpublished.

obi-kawasi-nickel-hpal.conditions_add: The amended and restated Pledge of Shares Agreement over PT Halmahera Persada Lygend, filed on the Hong Kong exchange, sets out parts of the "US$605,000,000 (or in any case not exceeding US$625,000,000 post accordion) Facilities Agreement dated 22 February 2021", under which "the Expansion Lenders have agreed to make available additional term loan facility of up to US$186,500,000" so that "the Total Commitment is up to US$811,500,000". Clause 5.2(a) says "The Pledgor must procure that the Borrower will comply with the dividend treatment as provided in clause 14.3" "(Distribution Conditions) of the Cash and Accounts Management Agreement." The pledgor is the Indonesian parent PT Trimegah Bangun Persada; PT Bank DBS Indonesia is the agent, BNP Paribas the technical and modelling bank and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk the security agent and pledgee. The Cash and Accounts Management Agreement is not filed, so what the dividend treatment itself requires cannot be read.

why.fincov: "The Pledgor must procure that the Borrower will comply with the dividend treatment as provided in clause 14.3" "(Distribution Conditions) of the Cash and Accounts Management Agreement."

sources_add.title: Amended and Restated Pledge of Shares Agreement over shares in PT Halmahera Persada Lygend

obi-kawasi-nickel-hpal.searched: The pledge agreement on HKEXnews was opened and read: it gives the Facilities Agreement's date, size and parties and the obligation to procure the borrower's compliance with the Distribution Conditions of the Cash and Accounts Management Agreement. The clause-4 wording about perfecting the pledged shares "as part of the conditions subsequent in the Facilities Agreement" has been dropped as ordinary security mechanics, the same ground round 8 left untyped for Obi's share pledges and completion guarantee. The Facilities Agreement, the Cash and Accounts Management Agreement and the Equity Support and Retention Deed are referred to but not filed, so the use-of-proceeds wording and the lender list in Schedule 1 could not be read.

kilombero-plantations-agrica.searched: Tried the financiers' own disclosure rather than the Oakland Institute report: BIO-style investment pages, Norfund's published investment data, the AECF grant announcement and the UK aid records surfaced only amounts and purposes. No DFID business case, AgDevCo loan paper or Norfund agreement for Kilombero Plantations was found, and the FAO case study describes the farm's operations, not a financier's term.

jirau-dam-esbr-madeira.searched: No new document was found on the private side. GDF Suez's 2014 green bond eligibility rule is the issuer's own framework, not a lender's condition, and no prospectus, BNDES on-lending contract clause or arbitration filing tying the bond or shareholder money to a requirement was found. Correction to the earlier note: recommon.org is not a refusing host - its English homepage serves in full - the failure was on the particular page sought.

proyecto-integral-morelos-samir-flores.searched: Searched Spanish government and company sources for the FIEM operation rather than the Elecnor release: the Council of Ministers references on lamoncloa.gob.es and the FIEM credit-line documents on comercio.gob.es set out the fund's general rules only, with no published approval naming the Morelos pipeline, and the Jones Day note on the Banamex/Banobras/ICO loan describes the deal without quoting a covenant. No FIEM loan agreement for this project is published.

chitwan-wwf-ranger-custody-death.searched: No document type reaches a grant funder here. WWF publishes no grant agreement for WWF Nepal's anti-poaching support, its US tax filings carry no schedule of terms for this programme, and no Nepali court or inquiry filing quoting an agreement was found. Hosts that refused in the earlier round: buzzfeednews.com, kathmandupost.com.

kinangop-wind-park-shooting.searched: Searched for the Standard Bank and CfC Stanbic facility papers and for Norfund and Africa Infrastructure Investment Fund II disclosures on the written-off investment. Only investment and write-off announcements were found; no facility agreement, environmental and social action plan or covenant for the US$90 million debt is published.

wwf-cameroon-baka-ecoguards.searched: No new route exists. WWF publishes no grant agreement with the Cameroonian ministry for ecoguard support, the 2020 independent panel report describes practice rather than funding terms, and no tax schedule or court filing setting a condition was found.

african-parks-odzala-baka.searched: African Parks' management agreement with the Republic of the Congo is still unpublished, and the organisation's annual reports and its 2025 response to the independent investigation set out no condition attached to its money. No filing, grant agreement or court document was found.

rapu-rapu-cyanide-spills-2005.searched: Went round the paywalled mining trade press to the Philippine daily coverage of the creditors: the Philippine Star report of 15 May 2006 names the syndicate - N.M. Rothschild & Sons (Australia), ANZ, ABN AMRO Bank NV (Australia), Investec Bank (Mauritius) and Standard Chartered First Bank Korea - and a US$35 million debt facility with an A$140 million hedge mark-to-market exposure and an A$60 million metal forward liability, but no covenant, condition precedent or default trigger. The 21 conditions Lafayette says it met were set by Philippine government agencies, not by the lenders. Host that refused: miningnews.net (paywall).

santo-antonio-dam-madeira.searched: No term attached to Santander's or Banco Espirito Santo's own money is published. The requirements on record belong to BNDES, the Brazilian state bank whose funds Santander on-lent, so they cannot be written up as the foreign lender's condition, and BankTrack records only that the project was identified as an Equator Principles project, which is the banks' general framework.

batang-coal-jbic.searched: JBIC's own press release of 3 June 2016 and Itochu's release of the same date do serve (jbic.go.jp press pages, unlike its project pages). Both give the loan size - about US$2,052 million from JBIC inside a US$3,421 million co-financing with SMBC, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ, Mizuho, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust, Mitsubishi UFJ Trust, Shinsei, Norinchukin, DBS and OCBC - and say the Indonesia Infrastructure Guarantee Fund guarantees PLN's payment obligations under the 25-year power purchase agreement. Neither states a condition, covenant or environmental and social requirement attached to the loan, and neither says the loan depended on the IIGF guarantee. The loan also post-dates most of the land takeover.

balhaf-lng-detention-site.searched: Searched the project-finance record for the US$2.8 billion Yemen LNG facility of 2008 and the French export credit guarantees. Trade accounts and law-firm notes name the arrangers and record that the project reached 'lenders' completion' in 2012, but no facility agreement, bond prospectus or arbitration award quoting a covenant was found, and the terms of the EUR 216 million French export credit guarantees are not published. The financing also closed years before the 2015-2018 use of the site.

tsumeb-smelter-arsenic.searched: No lender term can be attached to the smelter. The EBRD loans on record are for Dundee Precious Metals' Chelopech mine in Bulgaria, a different project, and under the brief's rule an intermediary or sister-project term is not a condition on this one. The 2010 purchase clause exempting Dundee from liability for earlier owners' damage is a term of the sale agreement with the seller, not of any lender's money, and no Dundee credit agreement naming Tsumeb was found.

scatec-los-prados-namasigue.searched: Looked for the CABEI loan paper from the Honduran side and for a development-bank mirror. The only solar financing documents that surfaced for the area are an EIB allocation to CABEI for an 80.8 MWp plant in Choluteca (EIB project 20140633) and an IDB Invest environmental and social action plan for a different park, ZIP INHDELVA at Choloma; neither names Fotovoltaica Los Prados, so neither can be attached to this project. No CABEI, Norfund or Scatec agreement for Los Prados is published.

tozzi-green-ihorombe.searched: Opened BIO's investment page for JTF Madagascar again and the Finnfund record: BIO discloses a EUR 2.9 million loan dated November 2019 (shown as EUR 2,937,500) and describes development outcomes only - no environmental and social action plan, covenant or condition. No side letter or agreement for the EUR 7.5 million combined BIO/Finnfund investment was found, and the 2012 and 2018 state land leases are the company's own arrangements with Madagascar.

korindo-papua-forest-clearing.searched: No use-of-proceeds tie exists. The money on record is general corporate lending - BNI loans to Korindo's agricultural division and a 2012 SMBC loan for a wood-chip company in Kalimantan - none of it documented as reaching the Papua plantations, so under the brief's rule on intermediaries and unlinked facilities nothing can be attached. No facility agreement, bond prospectus or exchange filing setting a condition was found.

sakhalin-2-aniva-bay.searched: The JBIC-led Phase 2 loan was signed in June 2008, after the dredging and the blockades, so a covenant in it would post-date the harm. No term for the earlier Phase 1 financing by JBIC's predecessor was found in JBIC's press releases, the Friends of the Earth Japan timeline or the Bankwatch record, and the EBRD, US EXIM and ECGD never lent, so they set no terms.

indofood-lonsum-bank-financing.searched: No new document changes this. The money reported is general corporate lending and underwriting to Indofood and Indofood CBP, with no use-of-proceeds tie to a plantation and none of it documented as reaching London Sumatra, so under the brief's rule it cannot be written up as a condition on this site. No facility agreement, prospectus covenant or securities exhibit was found.

para-beef-banks-sao-felix.searched: No new document changes this. The money is general corporate lending and bond underwriting to JBS, Marfrig and Minerva, not tied to a ranch; the Marfrig transition bond framework is the issuer's own rule rather than a lender's condition. No facility agreement or prospectus covenant tying any of it to a sourcing requirement was found.

dabhol-enron-guhagar.searched: Tried the claims, arbitration and Indian official routes rather than Human Rights Watch. The Trans-Lex reprint of the Bechtel and GE arbitration against OPIC quotes only the insurance policy's exclusions, not the Phase I loan's terms; the OPIC Memorandum of Determinations on the Bank of America as Trustee claim is behind the Transnational Dispute Management paywall and the archived OPIC FOIA award PDF on webharvest.gov returned a rate-limit page again. A Prayas compilation of Maharashtra power documents (energy.prayaspune.org) records a GoI Support Agreement and a GoM Support Agreement for Phase I but states no purpose, and the only report of lenders demanding escrow cover and a larger letter of credit is a Business Standard piece of 2001, four years after the police actions. No Phase I financing agreement or Export-Import Bank or OPIC term sheet is published.

kaziranga-wwf-guards-shootings.searched: No document type reaches this funder. No memorandum of understanding between WWF India and the Assam Forest Department is published, WWF's tax filings carry no schedule of terms for the park support, and no Indian court or inquiry filing setting a condition on the equipment and funding was found.

tbla-dgs-mufg-danamon-peat.searched: The only term reported is MUFG's bank-wide no-deforestation, no-peat, no-exploitation policy, which is a general policy rather than a condition on these loans, and MUFG's majority stake in Bank Danamon makes Danamon an intermediary whose own lending terms are not documented for this borrower. No facility agreement, Bank Danamon filing or Tunas Baru Lampung exchange disclosure setting a condition was found.

enb-tobar-maybank-watwat.searched: Maybank still declines to confirm the relationship, the Papua New Guinea Investment Promotion Authority filings that Global Witness describes are not published online, and no facility agreement, court document or exchange filing quoting the July 2015 US$40 million line's terms was found. Nothing dates the line to the 2018-2019 raid either.

hongsa-lignite-thai-banks.searched: Tried the rating-agency route that worked for Xayaburi: TRIS Rating publishes no report on Hongsa Power Company, and its reports on RATCH Group treat Hongsa only as an equity investment and dividend source, with no loan covenant. The trade report already on file gives the facility's commercial terms - the EGAT offtake contract, a 75:25 debt-to-equity split, an 18-year tenor, repayment starting a year after operations and step-up and step-down margins - which are the facility's own pricing and structure rather than requirements on how the money was used. No loan agreement from the nine Thai lenders is published.

phnom-penh-sugar-kampong-speu.searched: Opened the Australian National Contact Point's final statement on the complaint (ausncp.gov.au, complaint 11) in full. It records that ANZ accepts "its due diligence on the project funded by its loan was inadequate" and that after 2014 it "encouraged its customer to address the adverse human rights impacts" without success, but it does not name Phnom Penh Sugar, give the loan's date or amount, or set out any covenant or requirement attached to it. No ANZ facility agreement has been published.
